claims.text: POL-NS-23 requires the driver, before cancelling for no-show, to have BOTH sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call before trip_record.cancelled_at. The trip record shows only the call limb met: a single in-app call placed at 12:49:20, ringing 22 s and unanswered. No in-app chat message from the driver at any point before the 12:53:20 cancellation appears on the record. The message limb therefore fails, and POL-NS-23 voids the fee — the rider is not to be charged, so the fee cannot be reinstated at the driver's request.

The chat export EV-CHAT-06065 is impaired: issue code TRUNCATED_LOG, weight multiplier 0.6, holding 1 of the trip record's 3 entries and nothing after 12:41:30, so it does not cover the arrival or the waiting window. On that impaired log the trip record's own derivation records contact_before_cancel.message_count = 0 with complete = false. Disclosed as impaired, the only driver contact the record establishes is the unanswered call; the record does not establish that the driver messaged the rider before cancelling.

If the Tribunal reads the message limb as not established rather than as absent, the very fact POL-NS-23 needs — whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling — cannot be established, because the chat log that would carry it is impaired (TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6). POL-GEN-26 directs escalation in exactly that situation, and on escalation no monetary outcome issues and the 5.00 SGD is held rather than returned to the driver, so the driver's claim still fails.

This dispute was filed by the driver, and the fare breakdown records the 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (payment_status REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 5.00). Under POL-GEN-03 outcomes are party-relative: the rider-favourable outcome here is NO_ACTION — the driver's claim is not supported and the present refunded state stands. FULL_REFUND is defined against the filing party and would move the money back to the driver, which is not the rider's case and is not sought.

The driver did clear POL-NS-21's free wait — auto-arrival at 12:46:50, cancellation at 12:53:20, 390 s later, past the 300 s free wait — and the arrival itself is not contested. But POL-NS-21's wait and POL-NS-23's contact obligation are cumulative conditions on the fee, not alternatives: clearing the wait does not cure the unmet message limb.

The rider engaged the in-app channel before the cancellation: her message of 12:41:30, read by the driver at 12:41:38, places her at the lobby and asks to be called on arrival. On this impaired export (TRUNCATED_LOG, weight 0.6) that is the only preserved entry, but it shows the driver had both notice and an open in-app channel throughout the wait; the record shows a call placed and no message sent in reply.

POL-NS-25's referral turns on rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d. The rider profile snapshot at filing does not carry that field, and POL-NS-25 applies only where it is present, so no repeat-no-show flag may be entered against the rider on this trip.

claims.text: The driver arrived at the pickup point and the GPS trace corroborates it. The trip record's driver_arrived event is 12:46:50, and the arrival check in the trace returns corroborated=true: the nearest fix sits 3.491261642503293 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 4 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. He cancelled at 12:53:20, 390 s after arrival, past the 300 s free wait that ran from arrival and expired at 12:51:50. The free-wait condition for a no-show cancellation under POL-NS-21 is therefore satisfied on this trip's own evidence.

Because the driver cancelled only after the free wait had expired, POL-NS-22 directs that the 5.00 SGD no-show fee be charged to the rider and transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. The payments ledger shows a cancellation_fee of 5.00 SGD that matches the policy fee exactly (fee_matches_policy=true, policy_fee_sgd=5.00, driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd=5.00). On the driver's case the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both at 5.00.

POL-NS-23's call limb is met on the platform's own telemetry. The rider's own 12:41:30 message asked the driver to 'call me when you're here', and trip_record.in_app_calls records exactly that: one in-app call placed by the driver at 12:49:20, before trip_record.cancelled_at of 12:53:20, ringing 22 s unanswered. The rider's counter-statement concedes the limb in terms - 'He called once.'

The message limb of POL-NS-23 cannot be held against the driver on this record. The chat log is IMPAIRED: issue code TRUNCATED_LOG fired, weight_multiplier is 0.6, because only 1 of the 3 entries that trip_record.chat_message_count records was exported, and the single surviving entry is the rider's own 12:41:30 message - nothing after 12:41:30 was preserved, so the export covers neither the arrival nor any part of the waiting window. The driver's filing asserts he messaged. I disclose that impairment, its weight and its issue code under POL-GEN-02(1): a 0.6-weight truncated export cannot establish a POL-NS-23 breach, so the fee is not voided.

POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring a fact from absent evidence. The chat export dumps nothing after 12:41:30, so the absence of a driver message within it proves only that the export is incomplete, not that no message was sent; the derived contact_before_cancel block itself records the reason as the log being 'MISSING or TRUNCATED'. POL-NS-23's 'if either is missing' limb is therefore not triggered on this record, and the fee stands.

The 5.00 SGD sits with the rider only because of the 13:32:20 entry - an 'interim reversal after a rider complaint: SGD 5.00 refunded to rider and withheld from driver pending review' - a provisional step, not an adjudication of the no-show. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative: it would leave that provisional refund standing and the driver out of pocket for a trip he worked. DRIVER_COMPENSATION is the outcome that moves the 5.00 SGD to the driver, and it is available to the tribunal under POL-GEN-03.

If the tribunal treats the message fact as unestablished rather than as established against the driver, the consequence is POL-GEN-26 escalation, not a voiding of the fee. The open question is whether the driver's messages, absent from the truncated export, were in fact sent; an escalated fee is held rather than refunded while a human reviews it, which is the only outcome on this record better for the driver than leaving the provisional refund in place.

ruling.explanation:
This is the driver's filing. He asks that the 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from him after her complaint be moved back to him. Both of the outcomes the parties argue for turn on one question the record cannot settle, and for that reason the case goes to a human reviewer.

What is agreed and established on both sides. The driver arrived at Block 9, Selegie Road at 12:46:50 — the GPS trace corroborates the trip record's arrival event, the nearest fix sitting 3.49 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 4 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (POL-NS-21). He cancelled at 12:53:20, 390 s after arrival, past the 300 s free wait that ran from arrival and expired at 12:51:50. POL-NS-21's free-wait condition and POL-NS-22's timing condition are therefore met. The call limb of POL-NS-23 is also met: the trip record's in_app_calls shows one in-app call placed by the driver at 12:49:20, before cancellation.

What is not decided — POL-NS-23's message limb. POL-NS-23 voids the 5.00 SGD fee if the driver did not also send at least one in-app chat message before cancelling. That fact cannot be read from this record. The chat log EV-CHAT-06065 is impaired: issue code TRUNCATED_LOG fired and its weight multiplier is 0.6. It holds 1 of the 3 entries the trip record counts, and nothing after 12:41:30, so it covers neither the arrival nor any part of the waiting window in which a pre-cancellation message would sit. The platform's own derivation says the same: contact_before_cancel.complete = false, message_count = 0, reason that the log is missing or truncated. The rider's account that the driver “never messaged where he was” does not fill the gap — POL-NS-23's test reads the chat log and the trip record, not a party's account, and where the log admitted no reading over the relevant stretch an account stands in for the test rather than supplementing it. So the message limb is undecided: it supports neither moving the 5.00 SGD back to the driver (which needs the contact obligation to hold) nor confirming the refund to the rider (which needs it to have failed).

Because the fact POL-NS-23 needs — whether the driver messaged and called before cancelling — cannot be established on evidence that is impaired, POL-GEN-26 sends the case to human review, and POL-NS-26 itself carves this out from the AI's final say on a no-show. The ruling is ESCALATE: this ruling moves no money, and the 5.00 SGD already refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver (fare breakdown: payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00; the 13:32:20 fee_reversed event) is held for the reviewer.

On the remaining points. The fee charged is 5.00 SGD, matching POL-NS-22's policy fee, so the fee-amount referral does not arise. The driver did attempt contact, by the 12:49:20 call, so POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not fire. The rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d field, and POL-NS-25 applies only where it is present, so no repeat-no-show flag is entered. Referrals are therefore empty.

Confidence is 0.6 — the weight of the impaired chat log, which is the only artifact that would carry the undecided message fact. The disputed value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and no fraud flag is carried by either profile, so the confidence bar is not the obstacle here; POL-GEN-26 is.

Open question for the reviewer: did the driver send an in-app chat message before cancelling at 12:53:20? The full chat export (3 messages per the trip record) will settle whether POL-NS-23 voids the fee or leaves it standing.
